claim: LLMs are systematically overconfident when verbalizing their confidence, potentially imitating human patterns of confidence expression rather than reflecting true predictive uncertainty.
stance_target: verbal confidence elicitation is unreliable as a calibration signal
scope_conditions: 5 dataset types (commonsense, arithmetic reasoning, etc.), 5 LLMs including GPT-4 and LLaMA 2 Chat; ICLR 2024
quoted_support: LLMs, when verbalizing their confidence, tend to be overconfident, potentially imitating human patterns of expressing confidence.

claim: White-box (internal-state-based) confidence elicitation methods outperform black-box verbal-confidence methods, but the gap is narrow, with reported AUROC ranging from 0.522 to 0.605 across the evaluated black-box methods.
stance_target: the achievable AUROC ceiling for verbal/black-box confidence elicitation on standard reasoning benchmarks
scope_conditions: 5 LLMs, 5 dataset types, black-box vs white-box comparison
quoted_support: Comparisons with white-box methods indicate that while white-box methods perform better, the gap is narrow, e.g., 0.522 to 0.605 in AUROC.

claim: No single confidence elicitation technique (prompting strategy, sampling method, or aggregation technique) consistently outperforms others, and all investigated methods struggle on challenging tasks requiring professional knowledge.
stance_target: any single confidence-elicitation protocol being a universally superior, benchmark-independent method
scope_conditions: systematic framework spanning prompting x sampling x aggregation across 5 datasets and 5 models
quoted_support: none of these techniques consistently outperform others, and all investigated methods struggle in challenging tasks, such as those requiring professional knowledge, indicating significant scope for improvement.

claim: As model capability scales up, both confidence calibration and failure prediction performance improve.
stance_target: relationship between model scale and calibration/failure-prediction quality
scope_conditions: 5 widely-used LLMs of varying scale evaluated on calibration and failure-prediction tasks
quoted_support: As model capability scales up, both calibration and failure prediction performance improve.
